title: Adaptive tenant-priority prefetching and smart page-stitching for dashboard query API
creator: Maya Chen
description: Problem: Console dashboard query API exhibits tail latency and high read amplification for interactive explorations across large tenants. Current cursor pagination pulls full page windows and performs symmetric index scans that amplify cost for tenants with sparse active time series. Goal: reduce 95th/99th percentile query latency for paginated listing endpoints while keeping per-tenant read amplification under a 2x budget and preserving deterministic cursor semantics for end-users. This ticket designs and implements a combined tenant-priority prefetcher and smart page-stitching layer in the dashboard query API to: 1) prioritize small, low-latency prefetched windows for customers flagged as high-SLO; 2) stitch together sparse pages on the server-side to avoid issuing multiple round-trips for common UX patterns (fast next/prev navigation); 3) integrate with shard-aware index hints so the storage layer can avoid hot-scan amplification. We will implement telemetry to measure cost delta and a canary rollout gating by tenant-class.
acceptance_criteria: 95th percentile single-page fetch latency reduced by >= 25% for interactive queries (measured on sampled tenant cohort)
Per-tenant read amplification (IO pages accessed per result row) reduced to <= 2.0 for targeted workloads compared to baseline
No regression in correctness: cursor semantics remain stable and ordering is identical to current API for identical parameters
Rollout path established: canary to 5% of high-SLO tenants then 50% then global with rollback metric thresholds
Instrumentation surfaces: token-level cost estimate, per-request shard hit ratio, prefetch hit/miss rate available in Console observability dashboards
implementation_plan: Design prefetch policy: per-tenant priority score (SLO tier, recent activity vector, estimated result density) and budgeted prefetch window size
Add Smart Page-Stitcher middleware in query API that can merge adjacent sparse pages into single responses when client requests sequential navigation patterns (next/prev) within a short TTL
Expose index-hint header from API to storage layer: prefer 'shard-aware-range' vs 'global-scan' modes based on tenant density estimate
Implement adaptive hedging: issue a hedged read to a secondary replica only if primary latency exceeds a dialed threshold AND budget allows
Add metrics and tracing: prefetch_bytes, prefetch_rows, stitch_count, stitch_latency, read_amplification_estimate, hedged_reads
Benchmark in perf lab with synthetic tenants (sparse, dense, bursty) and compare against baseline workload generator
Create DB migration / config flag to gate new behavior per-tenant and implement rollout orchestration in Console (canary service)
Ship PR with feature gate behind runtime flag and add e2e tests for cursor correctness and stitch scenarios
risk_and_mitigation: Risk: server-side stitching may increase CPU and response size leading to higher p95 for large-result queries. Mitigation: enforce stitch size cap and cost-based throttling per request.
Risk: prefetching could increase I/O for low-value tenants. Mitigation: conservative default budgets with warmup annealing and per-tenant opt-out via rollout config.
Risk: hedged reads could double IO if misconfigured. Mitigation: gated on observed tail latency and limited concurrency; add automatic rollback on cost delta > 30%.
Risk: cursor incompatibilities. Mitigation: maintain canonical cursor encoding and add regression tests; opt-in migration with logging for mismatches.
